::: {.block title="Methods"}
We trained a separate boosted regression tree (BRT)[^brt] for each 10 m depth bin from the surface to 200 m to predict $\log_{10}(\mathrm{Chl}\,a)$ from remote-sensing reflectance ($R_{rs}$) using 11 or 172 bands, local solar hour, and sampling platform. Local solar hour allowed the model to account for daytime quenching of in situ chlorophyll fluorescence. Each profile was matched to the nearest grid cell in the same-day Level-3 $R_{rs}$ map. We evaluated out-of-sample skill using five repeats of grouped fivefold cross-validation, keeping all profiles within each 1° × 30-day block in the same fold.  [^brt]: Neural networks yielded higher skill, but for this pilot study, we used BRTs for their shorter training time.
:::
